answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: a node’s influence is the walk’s probability mass, not its declared identities. A Sybil cluster typically attaches through a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits escape and, by min-cut transitivity bounds, constrains aggregate voting weight to the cut’s attested capacity. Thus no fable, sable, or gale of aliases can amplify support without costly honest attestations.
